summary: Cibola/Lincoln NF lookout on Gallinas Peak, erected 1933 on a 46-ft steel Aermotor tower; NHLR-registered 2007; standing, with a road to the summit.

facts.design: 7x7 ft MC-39 cab on a 46-ft steel Aermotor tower, part of a complex with an observer's cabin and tool shed

access.note: A road reaches the summit. I could not confirm whether the tower or cab is open to visitors.

visit.trail_note: No trails in this part of the forest; forest roads reach the summit

events.note: Construction of a telephone line for the Gallinas lookout
September 1932 newspaper: new steel towers replaced worn-out wooden ones, including a 48-ft tower on Gallinas
June 1932: fire guard Paul Porter injured in a fall from the ladder to the lookout tower
Erected in 1933 as a 7x7 ft MC-39 cab on a 46-ft steel tower (2020 chapter report); a June 1933 newspaper item reports a new tower erected
Remodeling and improvements completed on the Gallinas, Wofford and Mayhill towers and cabins (newspaper spellings)
Fires ravaged the mountain; the summit was spared
Registered June 17, 2007; nominated by Dave Lorenz; described as recently returned to active service
Not evaluated in the 1988 thematic NRHP nomination; the 2020 chapter report says it should be evaluated and nominated if eligible

corrections.why: The register and the 2020 chapter report both give a 46-ft steel tower, about 14.0 m. The brief's 15.2 m is 50 ft, a height that the 1933 newspaper gave for a tower staked out at the site.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Newspapers from 1932-1933 give 48 ft (placed), 40 ft (shipped) and 50 ft (staked). The register and the 2020 report give 46 ft. The story uses 46 ft and reports the newspaper figures.
A September 1932 item says new steel towers replaced worn-out wooden ones, including on Gallinas. The 2020 report and a June 1933 item date the present tower to 1933. The story reports both dates.

notes_for_editor: Current staffing and visitor access are unconfirmed. Access level restricted is a judgment: the summit road is open, but the tower and cab are not confirmed open. SummitPost is a crowd-sourced climbing site, used only for road, summit and 2004 fire statements. Name spellings vary (Galilnas in FFLA, Gallinas in NHLR, Galinas in the 1938 newspaper).
